domain: German federal zoonoses monitoring - sample-level food pathogen detection prediction (national sector-regulator publisher, EU member state)
prediction_question: For a food sample drawn under the German zoonoses monitoring programme (Zoonosen-Monitoring, ZooM) from a stated matrix, will it test positive for Campylobacter spp., given only the sampling-plan and item attributes decided when the sample is taken: reporting year, sampling date/month, matrix and matrix group, sampling stage (slaughterhouse/retail etc.), production type (conventional/organic), origin country, processing (chilled/frozen...), packaging, and programme?
prediction_time: The moment the sample is taken: every feature is an attribute of the sampling plan or of the sampled item as recorded at sampling (Jahr, PNDat, MatrixGr/Matrix, Betriebsart, ZusA, HerkStaat, Verarbeitung, Verpackung, PNMG); the label is the laboratory result reported afterwards (ErgAlphaT 'positiv; nachgewiesen' / 'negativ; nicht nachgewiesen' from the programme's standardised qualitative detection methods). No post-hoc field is needed as a feature. A secondary parameter family with the same timing (ESBL/AmpC-bildende E. coli) is measured as a fallback in case Campylobacter proves too thin at construction.
target_definition: Binary from the source row: ErgAlphaT = 'positiv; nachgewiesen' (detected) vs 'negativ; nicht nachgewiesen' (not detected), restricted to rows whose Parameter is the Campylobacter genus detection ('Genus Campylobacter'; Parameter/ParameterT1 columns). Label source columns ErgAlpha, ErgAlphaT and the legally derived assessment Bewertung/BewertungT ('Beanstandet'/'Ohne Beanstandung') are recorded in label_source_columns and must be absent from the shipped features. Unit/frame: qualitative presence/absence per sample at the method's declared analytical amount (Methode/Probenvorbereitung columns, e.g. 10 g), the publisher's own frame - no external threshold is compared, so no known-event fixture is required. Rows where a quantitative result or a different parameter vocabulary appears are out of frame and must be pinned at construction from the Datensatzbeschreibung column dictionary.

construction_script: planned: candidates/bvl-zoom-sample-positivity/source/build.py (stdlib only; downloads the three year zips, filters to the Campylobacter genus parameter, feature columns from the sampling-plan fields, label from ErgAlphaT, runner layout + qualification gate)
split_strategy: Temporal, one row per (sample x reporting year) in the Campylobacter frame: train 2021, eval 2022, holdout 2023 - the only three reporting years the publisher exposes. Measured on the downloaded CSVs (2026-10-21): Campylobacter genus rows 2021: 1,394 rows / 443 positive (31.8%); 2022: 2,364 / 613 (25.9%); 2023: 1,312 / 390 (29.7%) - both classes present in every window, so the split-capacity contract is satisfied as measured, but each window is a single reporting year (thin depth; no second holdout year exists yet). Positives cluster by sampling batch/day: distinct samples per year are 5,373 (2021) and 5,969 (2022), but the ProbenNrPseud column is EMPTY in the 2023 file (measured: 0 distinct values vs thousands in 2021/2022) - a publisher data-quality defect that forces 2023 clustering to fall back to matrix x month proxies, and construction must report the clustered count under that limitation. Fallback parameter with the same timing if Campylobacter is too thin: ESBL/AmpC-bildende E. coli 1,947/1,900/1,825 rows at 32.3%/19.8%/26.4%.

measurements.year_zips_2026_10_21: GET 2021 zip -> 200, 418,430 B; 2022 -> 200, 532,407 B; 2023 -> 200, 330,490 B; HEAD probes for 2020/2024/2025 URL patterns -> HTTP 404. Each zip: one cp1252 semicolon CSV (quoted fields with embedded semicolons - a naive split(';') parse misreads rows, measured).
measurements.grain_and_counts_2026_10_21: (sample x parameter) rows: 2021: 22,224 rows / 5,373 distinct ProbenNrPseud; 2022: 27,347 / 5,969; 2023: 22,349 / 0 (sample ID column blank). 49 columns per the Datensatzbeschreibung.
measurements.campylobacter_frame_2026_10_21: Proper csv parse (delimiter=';', quotechar='"'): 'Genus Campylobacter' rows 1,394 (2021, 443 positive, 31.8%), 2,364 (2022, 613, 25.9%), 1,312 (2023, 390, 29.7%). Matrix-level 2021 rates show real structure beyond a single base rate: chicken parts 41.8% genus-level (871 rows), chicken breast 15.7% (248), Campylobacter jejuni 71.7% (364), C. coli 76.0% (346) - species-level parameters are confirmatory follow-ups on genus-positive or enrichment samples and must NOT be pooled with genus rows.
measurements.other_parameters_2026_10_21: Measured per-year rates for alternative frames: Listeria monocytogenes 7.0%/10.2%/3.9% (2,140/2,329/2,932 rows); Salmonella genus 2.2%/7.4%/2.1% (2,220/3,454/2,491); E. coli ESBL/AmpC 32.3%/19.8%/26.4%; STEC (verotoxinbildende E. coli) 4.3%/9.4% (2021/2023); MRSA-verdaechtig 5.3%/11.4%/15.5%.
measurements.sampling_dates_2026_10_21: PNDat carries ddMMMyy-style SAS dates (e.g. 30MAY23:00:00:00) - month-of-year features are derivable; months spread across the year (APR/MAY/JUN/JUL/SEP observed in sample rows), supporting seasonality as a real feature.
measurements.novelty_risk_note: Matrix dominates the base rate (chicken-family matrices ~15-70% vs ~0 for beef/leaf matrices), so the reference baseline will be a matrix-stratified rate; the task's headroom over that baseline (season, stage, origin, production type) is the measured question at construction, as with flunet's persistence baseline.

next_action: Construction (advancement session): read the Datensatzbeschreibung PDF column-by-column and pin every feature's documented meaning; write source/build.py (three year zips -> Campylobacter frame -> runner layout + gate on a worker); decide the 2023 clustering proxy (ProbenNrPseud is blank there) and report clustered positive counts; cross-check the built frame against the BVL national ZooM annual report's published Campylobacter prevalence figures (the publisher's summary product, e.g. Zoonosen_Monitoring_Bericht_2023.pdf, already linked from the catalogue record); record the matrix-stratified rate as the reference baseline a solver must beat. Risks to carry: only three reporting years exist (one per split window), the 2024/2025 files 404 as of 2026-10-21 (refresh cadence lagging - re-probe quarterly, it would deepen holdout), and the 2023 blank sample-ID defect.

prior_art: EFSA/EU baseline survey prevalence summaries and the BVL annual ZooM reports (aggregate statistics, not prediction tasks); Campylobacter risk-factor literature (farm-level studies); no public sample-level monitoring-positivity benchmark found
novelty_check.theirs: The publisher (BVL) publishes the raw sample-parameter records per reporting year and prevalence summaries in national/EU zoonoses reports (EFSA One Health reports aggregate prevalence by category); risk-factor literature models Campylobacter in broiler flocks at farm level, not a released prediction task with splits.
novelty_check.ours: A binary sample-level detection task on the German zoonoses monitoring open data (will a monitoring sample from a stated matrix test positive for Campylobacter spp.), with disjoint reporting-year splits (2021/2022/2023 - the only years published), features restricted to sampling-plan attributes decided when the sample is taken, and a scored contract for coding-agent evaluation. No ML-ready version of this formulation exists in public catalogs.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
